unit.title: Angles and Constructions
unit.blurb: Corresponding and alternate angles on parallel lines, the exterior angle of a triangle, and ruler-and-compasses constructions.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Recognise corresponding, alternate and vertically opposite angles on parallel lines and use them to find angles.

O2.t: Use the fact that the exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles.

O3.t: Construct perpendicular bisectors, angle bisectors and triangles with ruler and compasses.

lesson.t: What angles are made when a line crosses parallel lines?
p: A line that crosses two parallel lines is called a **transversal**. It makes eight angles (a to h in the diagram), in two groups of equal angles.
**Corresponding angles are equal** – they are in the same position at each crossing (an **F** shape).
**Alternate angles are equal** – they are on opposite sides of the transversal, between the parallel lines (a **Z** shape).
**Co-interior angles add up to 180°** – they are on the same side, between the parallel lines (a **C** or U shape).
**Vertically opposite angles are equal** and **angles on a straight line add up to 180°** – at any crossing, parallel or not.
Corresponding, alternate and co-interior facts are **only true when the lines are parallel**.

lesson.t: How do I find angles on parallel lines?
p: Step 1: Mark the angle you know.
Step 2: Look for an F, Z or C shape that links it to the angle you want.
Step 3: Use equal (F, Z, vertically opposite) or add to 180° (C, straight line).
Step 4: Give the correct reason using the angle name.

sections.title: The exterior angle of a triangle

lesson.t: What is an exterior angle of a triangle?
p: If you extend one side of a triangle, the angle between the extension and the next side is an **exterior angle**.
The interior and exterior angles at the same vertex lie on a straight line, so they **add up to 180°**.

lesson.t: What is the exterior angle fact?
p: **The exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles.**
Why? Interior angles: a + b + c = 180°. Exterior angle at c: 180° − c = **a + b**.
In the diagram the interior angles shown are 50° and 70°, so the exterior angle at the third vertex is 120°.

lesson.t: How do I use the exterior angle fact?
p: Step 1: Identify the exterior angle and the two interior angles **opposite** to it (not the one next to it).
Step 2: Add the two opposite interior angles.
Step 3: Or, to find a missing interior angle: exterior − known opposite angle.

lesson.t: What constructions use ruler and compasses?
p: A **perpendicular bisector** of a line segment cuts it **in half at right angles**. Every point on it is the same distance from both ends.
An **angle bisector** cuts an angle **in half**. Every point on it is the same distance from both arms.
These constructions use only a straight edge and compasses, so they are exact.

lesson.t: How do I construct a perpendicular bisector of AB?
p: Open the compasses to **more than half** of AB. With the point on A, draw arcs above and below the line. Keep the same radius and repeat from B.
Join the two points where the arcs cross. This line meets AB at its midpoint M at 90°: if AB = 12 cm, AM = 6 cm.

lesson.t: How do I construct an angle bisector?
p: With the point on the vertex, draw an arc crossing both arms. From each crossing point, draw arcs (same radius) that meet inside the angle. Join the vertex to that meeting point.

lesson.t: How do I construct a triangle from three sides (SSS)?
p: Step 1: Draw the longest side with a ruler.
Step 2: Set the compasses to the second length and draw an arc from one end.
Step 3: Set them to the third length and draw an arc from the other end.
Step 4: Join both ends to where the arcs cross. Leave the arcs showing.
